1E2A.name: Cluster sprite Y position high
1E2A.kind: byte table, one per cluster sprite slot (index X)
desc: High byte of each cluster sprite's 16-bit Y position ($1E02 is the low byte). Set when a cluster sprite
is spawned (Boo ring, Boo/bat ceiling, bonus 1-up, Sumo Bro flames), then updated with carry as the
sprite moves; compared against the screen boundary when despawning or drawing.
The Keyhole and Sumo Bro flame code also store through the same table with a Y index.

1E3E.name: Cluster sprite X position high
1E3E.kind: byte table, one per cluster sprite slot (index X)
desc: High byte of each cluster sprite's 16-bit X position ($1E16 is the low byte). Set at spawn (spawn of
cluster type 8, level load, ring of Boos) as screen X high plus carry, and kept in step as the sprite
moves. Read by the Sumo Bro flame and bonus 1-up contact code, and by the despawn check.

1E52.name: Cluster sprite Y speed
1E52.kind: byte table, one per cluster sprite slot (index X), signed
desc: Vertical speed of each cluster sprite. Boo/bat ceiling sprites set it to an aimed speed plus 9 (a
downward bias); the bonus 1-up cluster sprite adds 3 per frame as gravity, up to $40.
Added into the Y position ($1E02 with $1E7A as the fraction) by the shared move helper.
Cluster type 5 spawns store a shifted table value here. Keyhole uses its copy as a timer ($10).

1E66.name: Cluster sprite X speed
1E66.kind: byte table, one per cluster sprite slot (index X), signed
desc: Horizontal speed of each cluster sprite. Boo/bat ceiling sprites set it to an aimed speed; the bonus
1-up cluster sprite negates it to bounce off walls. Cluster type 5 spawns store the high nibble of a
table value; type 8 spawns and level load clear it.
Applied to the X position ($1E16 with $1E8E as the fraction) by the cluster move helper.

1E7A.name: Cluster sprite Y fraction
1E7A.kind: byte table, one per cluster sprite slot (index X)
desc: Sub-pixel fraction of a cluster sprite's Y position. Each frame the cluster despawn/move helper adds
the Y speed ($1E52) times 16 (low nibble) into it and carries into the Y position ($1E02).
Cluster type 5 spawns initialise it from the low nibble of a table value, shifted up.

1EA2.name: Overworld level flags
1EA2.kind: bit flags table, one per translevel number (index X/Y)
desc: Per-level progress flags, indexed by translevel number ($13BF). It is the live copy of the saved
level data; save data is copied here on file load and copied back after each level.
Set when a level is cleared or its midway point is passed, and read by the overworld path code to
decide which exits are open and whether Mario may leave a level.
Bits: Bit 7: level beaten (clear = Mario cannot exit it, the game returns).
Bit 6: midway point reached. Bits 0-3: exit open on that side of the level tile (bits from DATA_04941E).

1EEB.name: Special Zone cleared flag
desc: Bit 7 is probably set once the Special Zone is cleared. Tested by the level sprite spawner, Net Koopa
and bounce sprite code to pick the alternate (post-Special World) palette/graphics, by the GFX upload
routine to load the post-special graphics file, and by the ending enemy scene.
Values: bit 7 clear = normal game; bit 7 set = Special World cleared (changed enemy colours).

1F02.name: Overworld events passed flags
1F02.kind: bit flags array (one bit per overworld event)
desc: Bit array of overworld events already triggered (path openings, switch palace tile changes). Event
number / 8 selects the byte, event number AND 7 selects the bit (mask table DATA_04E44B).
Tested when drawing or applying completed events to the layer 1 and layer 2 maps, and copied into
the save buffer after a level. An unused routine in bank 5 also tests it as a level-cleared flag.

1F11.name: Player's current submap
1F11.kind: byte table, one per player (index X/Y: Mario, Luigi)
desc: Which overworld submap each player is on. $1F11 is Mario, $1F12 Luigi; read through the active-player
index. Written when the overworld loads (0 = main Yoshi's Island map), on submap warps, and by the
message trigger sprite.
Read by level loading to pick the level for the OW tile, by the overworld drawing and DMA code to pick
map pages, and by Monty Mole, Yoshi, Hammer Bro and block code that behave per world.
Values: 0 = Yoshi's Island map; other values = other submaps (1 = Yoshi's Island in the cutscene list).

1F13.name: Player overworld animation
1F13.kind: byte table, one per player (X=0 Mario, 4 Luigi)
desc: Mario's/Luigi's overworld pose/animation: facing and walking direction frame used when drawing the
map sprite. Written while walking along a path and reset to 0 (standing) when the OW is prepared.
Read by the 2x2 player draw routine, the Yoshi-riding draw routine and the walk start/enter-level
code to decide which way the player faces.

1F17.name: Player overworld X position
1F17.kind: word (little endian), one per player (index 0 Mario, 4 Luigi)
desc: Player's X position on the overworld map in pixels (low byte; $1F18 is the high byte). Set from the
exit tables when leaving a level, at submap warps and when walking starts.
Mario's walk code compares it with the destination ($0DC7) to know the signed distance left.
Also read by the border icon, level-start and the overworld sprite helpers that home in on the player.

1F19.name: Player overworld Y position
1F19.kind: word (little endian), one per player (index 0 Mario, 4 Luigi)
desc: Player's Y position on the overworld map in pixels (low byte; $1F1A is the high byte). Set from the
exit tables when leaving a level, at submap warps and when walking starts, and updated as Mario walks.
Read by the overworld draw, level name, tile exit, and overworld sprite code (switch palace particles,
chasing sprites). The intro code also writes $8E to it once (purpose unclear).

1F1A.name: Player overworld Y position high
1F1A.kind: byte (high byte of the word at $1F19)
desc: High byte of Mario's overworld Y position ($1F19 is the low byte). The tile position routine adds $FF
plus carry each other frame so Mario moves up one pixel every second frame during the intro walk.
Read by the switch palace ! block particles and the overworld sprite that chases Mario.

1F1F.name: Player overworld tile X
1F1F.kind: byte table, one per player (index X: 0 Mario, 4 Luigi)
desc: Column of the overworld tile (map16 position) the player is standing on. Written when Mario
finishes a step along the path, when entering a level and when a tile's exit flag is set.
Read with $1F21 (tile Y) to look up the level number table at $7ED000 and the tile data, and compared
to find a warp tile.

1F21.name: Player overworld tile Y
1F21.kind: byte table, one per player (index X: 0 Mario, 4 Luigi)
desc: Row of the overworld tile the player is standing on; partner of $1F1F (tile column). Written when the
player steps onto a new tile, enters a level, warps submap, or a tile's exit flag is set.
Used to index the OW tile and level-number tables and to find warp tiles.

1F27.name: Switch palace pressed flags
1F27.kind: flag byte table, one per colour (index X)
desc: One byte for each colour switch (green, yellow, blue, red); non-zero once that switch has been hit.
Mario's block collision sets it to 1 when a switch block's ! switch is pressed (and does nothing if it
is already set). Level object code for the outline/solid switch blocks reads it to decide whether to
draw the dotted outline (0) or the solid block.
Values: 0 = not pressed yet; 1 = pressed.

1F2F.name: Five Yoshi coins collected bits
1F2F.kind: bit flags array, one bit per level
desc: Bit array of levels in which all 5 Yoshi coins were collected. Byte = translevel / 8 (index Y), bit =
translevel AND 7 (mask table DATA_0DA8A6). Set by block interaction when the fifth Yoshi coin is taken;
tested by the level object code to show the coin as already taken. Cleared at game start (mode 11).

1F3C.name: Invisible 1-up collected bits
1F3C.kind: bit flags array, one bit per level
desc: Bit array of levels where the hidden 1-up block has been collected. Byte = translevel / 8 (index Y),
bit = translevel AND 7. Set by block interaction when the 1-up is taken; tested when drawing
single-tile extended level objects so a collected one does not reappear.

1F49.name: Save data buffer
1F49.kind: byte array (working copy of the save file)
desc: Start of the working save data: a copy of the overworld/progress state, indexed by offset.
Loaded from SRAM on file select, initialised for a new file, shown by the Continue/End menu, written
back after a level, and copied to the live overworld state ($1EA2 onward) when the game starts.
Each routine just copies the byte at offset X/Y.

1FB8.name: Save copy of player 1 submap
desc: Save buffer copy of the overworld player state starting at $1F11 (submaps, animations, positions).
Initialised when a new file is created and, after a level, the current player's byte is copied to the
other player's. Also written by the message trigger sprite (set to 1).

1FE2.name: Sprite timer 7
1FE2.kind: byte table, one per sprite slot (index X)
desc: Extra countdown timer per sprite slot, counted down by the main sprite routine. Meaning depends on the
sprite type; a non-zero value disables something for a few frames.
Examples: kicked shell sets 5 (no cape contact), stunned sprites 8; Yoshi mount sets 2 (no-grab);
Rex half-squash timer ($0C); Sumo Bro lightning $10 (skip ground check); Koopa Kid/Chuck contact or
sound cooldown. Also tested by sprite-block interaction and the off-screen check. Cleared on spawn.
Values: 0 = timer expired / not running.

1FEB.name: Fireworks launch delay
desc: Used by the ending (Peach scene). Rocket spawning sets it to a delay value from a table before the
next firework can launch, and the controller does nothing while it is non-zero.
The ending picture routine also sets it to $80 (probably starts the credits).

1FEE.name: 3-up moon collected bits
1FEE.kind: bit flags array, one bit per level
desc: Bit array of levels where the 3-up moon has been collected. Byte = translevel / 8 (index Y), bit =
translevel AND 7. Set by block interaction when the moon is taken; tested when drawing the moon so it
does not reappear. Cleared at game start (mode 11).

1FFB.name: Lightning flash step count
desc: Remaining steps of the lightning flash. The Bowser room palette routine reads it as the current step
(0 = no flash running); the overworld sprite loop sets it from DATA_04F700 to start a flash.
Part of the lightning flash state with $1FFC (delay) and $1FFD (frames per step).

1FFC.name: Lightning flash delay
desc: Frames until the next lightning flash. Loaded from DATA_04F6F8[X] by the Bowser room palette routine
and by the overworld sprite loop. See $1FFB (steps) and $1FFD (frames per step).

1FFD.name: Lightning flash step timer
desc: Frames left in the current lightning flash step. Set to 8 for the first step by the Bowser room palette
routine and the overworld sprite loop; counted down by the same routines.
See $1FFB (step) and $1FFC (delay to the next flash).

1FFE.name: Credits palette/background reload request
desc: During the credits, non-zero asks the NMI handler to reload the palette when switching backgrounds.
The screen wipe update increments it to request the reload; the NMI tests it (only in the ending
cutscene), and the credits background DMA routine clears it once the reload is done.
Values: 0 = nothing requested.

7EB900.name: Overworld sprite X high / particles
desc: Probably the high byte of the X position of overworld sprites; the switch palace ! block particles
store the player's overworld X high ($1F18) here. Also written by level load buffer init (cleared).
Shares memory with the level buffers, so the meaning depends on game mode.

7EB978.name: Overworld sprite X low / particles
desc: Low byte of an overworld particle's X position. The switch palace ! block particles set it to the
player's overworld X ($1F17) when they are spawned.

7EB9F0.name: Overworld particle X speed
desc: Horizontal speed of an overworld particle. The switch palace ! block particles set it from
DATA_04F280[Y] so each particle flies in its own direction.

7EBA40.name: Overworld particle height speed
desc: Vertical (height) speed of an overworld particle. The switch palace ! block particles set it to $D0,
launching them upward, before gravity pulls them down.

7EC800.name: Overworld layer 1 tile map
7EC800.kind: byte array (tile number per map tile, index X)
desc: Overworld layer 1 map: one byte per 16x16 map tile, written by events and read for drawing and walking.
Filled at load, edited by overworld events (path reveals, switch palace changes), read for walking.
In levels the same RAM is the Map16 low byte buffer (written by Map16 setup, bridge breaking and
boss room tile animation, which stores the empty tile $25).

7ED000.name: Overworld level number table
7ED000.kind: byte array (index X, one per map tile)
desc: Level (translevel) number for each overworld map tile. Read by the level load, walking and exit code
at the player's tile position to find which level is entered. Initialised by the Map16 and level
buffer fill code (also the Map16 high byte buffer in levels).

7ED800.name: Overworld tile path flags
7ED800.kind: byte array (index X, one per map tile)
desc: Per-tile byte tested bitwise by direction (shifted right by [$08]) when the player starts walking
from a tile and when setting a level's exit flag. Probably marks which directions are open.
Initialised by the level buffer fill routine. Written only at setup, read-only otherwise.

7F0000.name: Overworld map attribute buffer
desc: Attribute (palette/flip) byte for each overworld map tile. Filled by the layer 1 map page drawing
(literal bytes) and read by the overworld event code when applying edits and fading tiles.

7F4000.name: Layer 2 tilemap buffer
desc: Tilemap buffer for overworld layer 2 (and the credits backgrounds). Written by the interleaved map
decompressor, by completed events on the layer 2 map, and by the credits code (top-left tile word,
masked by [$65]). Write-only in these routines; DMA uploads it to VRAM.

7F837B.name: Stripe image buffer write index
desc: Offset of the end of the VRAM stripe image buffer at $7F837D: where the next record will be written.
Every routine that queues text or tiles for VRAM (level name, message box, lives counter, tallies,
credits text, events, bridge break, cage block) reads it, writes records at that offset, and saves the
new end back. Cleared to 0 when the buffer is empty (it is flushed on NMI by the stripe uploader).

7F837D.name: Stripe image buffer: VRAM address high
7F837D.kind: byte, first byte of the stripe buffer (index X)
desc: Start of the VRAM stripe image buffer at $7F837D. Each record is: VRAM address high, VRAM address
low, flags/length (word), then tile data; $FF as the first byte ends the buffer.
Callers write the VRAM address high byte at [$7F837D+X], and $FF after the last record as the end
marker. $FF at the first byte means the buffer is empty.

7F837E.name: Stripe record VRAM address low
desc: Second byte of a stripe image record: low byte of the VRAM address the tile data is uploaded to.
The previous byte, $7F837D+X, is the high byte.

7F837F.name: Stripe record flags / length high
desc: Third byte of a stripe record: the high byte of the length word, together with flags (bit 6 = RLE,
bit 7 = vertical). 0 means horizontal, no RLE.
Callers also use it as the first data byte of the record ($7F8380 follows with the low length).

7F8380.name: Stripe record length low
desc: Fourth byte of a stripe record: the low byte of the data length minus 1 (e.g. $03 = 4 bytes, 2 tiles;
$0B = 12 bytes, 6 tiles). Written with the rest of the record header before the tile data.

7F8381.name: Stripe record tile data
7F8381.kind: byte, first data byte of a stripe record (index X)
desc: First data byte of record 1: the tile number of the first tile ($7F8382 holds its attributes).
Written by almost every stripe user for the first tile, and for the end marker $FF after the last
record (level name, tally digits replaced by a blank tile $38FC).

7F8382.name: Stripe record first tile attributes
desc: Attribute byte (YXPCCCTT) of the first tile of a record, following the tile number at $7F8381.
Commonly $39: palette 6, high priority, tile page 1 (level name, message box, lives counter,
file select digits).

7F8383.name: Stripe record second tile number
desc: Next data byte in a record after the first tile word: tile number of the second tile.
Written by Map16 tile generation, boss room tile animation, bridge breaking, lives counter, events
and cutscene code. File select overwrites the rest of the word with an empty tile.

7F8385.name: Stripe record 2 header / data
desc: Byte at offset 8 from the buffer start: start of a second stripe record when two records are queued
(VRAM address of the second row). Used by the bridge break code (header $0240 = RLE, count 2),
event tile drawing, and Map16 tile generation.
